pages.title: The nine-reading example
pages.text:
The nine-reading example
80, 62, 48, 40, 35, missing, 28, 25, 23.
At threshold 40:
N≤ = 5, N > = 3, N missing = 1.
The counter identity gives 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 .

Changing the threshold

change.

pages.title: The first recorded qualifying time
pages.text:
The ﬁrst recorded qualifying time
tﬁrst = min{ti : xi known and xi ≤ θ}.
For observations at integer minutes and θ = 40, tﬁrst = 3 min.

pages.title: Recorded time and continuous crossing
pages.text:
Recorded time and continuous crossing
The record contains T (2) = 48 and T (3) = 40 .
The ﬁrst qualifying observation occurs at
3 min. An exact continuous crossing requires a model between observations. With
oscillation, even earlier unobserved crossings are possible.

pages.title: Monotonicity of threshold counts
pages.text:
Monotonicity of threshold counts
{i : xi ≤ θ1} ⊆ { i : xi ≤ θ2} (θ1 ≤ θ2).
Therefore N≤(θ1) ≤ N≤(θ2).

pages.title: A loop with paired observations
pages.text:
A loop with paired observations
for time, value in zip(times, readings):
category = classify(value, target)
counts[category] += 1
if category == "at_or_below" and first is None:
first = time
Equal list lengths must be checked: zip stops at the shorter input.
